newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian bourse records big growth in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian bourse records big growth in 1996.

text.p: The Nigerian stock exchange recorded significant growth in market turnover in 1996 and is set to do even better this year, bourse chief executive Hayford Alile said on Friday.

Alile told a news conference that the market experienced growth in all areas. Some 882 million shares worth 7.058 billion naira were traded compared to 397 million shares valued at 1.838 billion naira in 1995.
"In volume terms, this performance represents 122.2 percent and in value terms 284 percent over the 1995 figures," Alile said.

He attributed the growth to policy changes during the year, namely introduction of a five percent price movement limit, review of share allocation system and reduction of settlement period to one from two weeks.
Alile said the all-share index which opened at 5092.15 on January 2, 1996 closed at 6992.10 on December 31, a 37.3 percent jump.
The new issues market also shot up by 16.1 percent. Some 36 new issues worth 21.45 billion naira were listed last year against 31 valued at 7.084 billion naira in 1995.
Alile said the introduction of a computerised settlement and custodian system in the first quarter of 1997 and an automated trading system later this year would further improve performance.
Activities would also be boosted with the expected privatisation of large public utilities this year, he said.
The market capitalisation of the exchange was 285.6 billion naira by end-December 1996, a 66.9 percent rise over 171.1 billion naira in 1995.
